docs/release-notes.md: "The public library and MCP `bridge_fsck` symbol names are unchanged." — yet the schema $id (a public identifier) silently changed
advisory.finding: The bridge_fsck schema `$id` was changed to `.../schemas/bridge/fsck.schema.json`, diverging from the universal `<filename>` convention (all other ~90 schemas have `$id` ending in their exact filename) while the file remains `bridge_fsck.schema.json`. `$id` is a public, stable wire identifier that the release notes claim is unchanged, and `schemas.registry()` keys resources by `$id`, so any future cross-file `$ref` in this schema would misresolve against a nonexistent `bridge/` base.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that the fsck/check-access/setup subparsers are help-only (drop the unused REMAINDER `args`, or add a comment that routing bypasses parse_args).
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:324: if args[0] in {"fsck", "check-access", "setup"}: ... return _passthrough(args[0], args[1:]) — intercepts before parse_args at line 329
src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:113: fsck.add_argument("args", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER) — never parsed
advisory.finding: The `fsck`/`check-access`/`setup` subparsers added in `_parser()` (each with `add_argument("args", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)`) are never used for argument parsing: `bridge_cli` intercepts these verbs at `args[0]` and dispatches to `_passthrough` before `parser.parse_args` is reached. The `REMAINDER` args are dead code and the subparsers exist only for the `format_help()` fallback, which misleadingly implies the parser handles these commands.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the help detection order-insensitive (scan all args for --help/-h) so `bridge fsck <opt> --help` does not trigger auto-init.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:325: if args[0] != "setup" and args[1:] in (["--help"], ["-h"]): — only matches when --help is the ONLY remaining arg
src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:180: is_help = bool(args and args[0] in {"--help", "-h"}) — inspects only the first token
src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:181-184: if not is_help and not config.tracker_dir_override(): ensure_initialized(init_only=False)
advisory.finding: `rebar bridge fsck --tickets-tracker=X --help` triggers tracker auto-initialization as a side effect of a help request: the help-only interception at line 325 requires `--help`/`-h` to be the sole argument, and `bridge_fsck_cli`'s `is_help` guard only inspects `args[0]`, so with a leading option `ensure_initialized(init_only=False)` runs before argparse processes `--help` and exits.
advisory.suggested_fix: Detect help via `any(a in {"--help","-h"} for a in args)` in both the interception and `bridge_fsck_cli`.

Convention across the package, e.g. src/rebar/schemas/fsck.schema.json:3: "$id": "https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/schemas/fsck.schema.json" — every other `$id` equals `.../schemas/<filename>.schema.json`

docs/api-stability.md:23 — the JSON Schemas are 'the same schemas advertised to MCP clients as outputSchema'; the `$id` is their externally-observable identity

ABSENCE: no `$ref` (found via search) targets either the old or new bridge_fsck `$id`, and bridge_fsck.schema.json contains no `$ref`, so $ref resolution does not break today; the concern is the silent, off-convention identifier change, not an immediate resolution failure
advisory.finding: The `bridge_fsck.schema.json` `$id` was changed to `https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/schemas/bridge/fsck.schema.json`, breaking the repo-wide convention (all ~110 other schemas use `$id` == `.../schemas/<exact-filename>.schema.json`). The file is still named `bridge_fsck.schema.json`, so its `$id` no longer matches its filename; the `$id` is the `referencing.Registry` resolution key (`schemas/__init__.py:403`) and the URI advertised to MCP clients as the schema identity. This identifier change is unrelated to the CLI-vocabulary migration and appears unintended.
advisory.suggested_fix: Restore `"$id": "https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/schemas/bridge_fsck.schema.json"` so the `$id` matches the filename and the rest of the schema package; the CLI-vocabulary migration does not require changing the schema identifier.
